headline: Quay Global remains selective and generally cautious on office REITs despite high replacement costs

He argues that 10-15 years of oversupply has sent vacancies skyrocketing, particularly on the US West Coast outside the Bay Area. He also points to higher leverage and questionable demand profiles as structural negatives for the office REIT sector, and notes limited growth avenues given minimal new construction.

So there's been a little bit of a boost there in the San Francisco office market. headline: Gavin Truong sees best-in-class US retail REITs as the most underappreciated opportunity in the global REIT sector, with rents up 40-50% and valuations still attractive

A key demand driver is that the top 10% of household incomes account for as much discretionary spending as the bottom 70%, and with rising stock market and house prices, wealthy consumers are spending heavily. This creates a tight leasing environment benefiting landlords.
